entries.note: rule-based; compartment holding abductor_pollicis_brevis, flexor_pollicis_brevis, opponens_pollicis (11.28 cm3), not split: APB, FPB and OP: the thenar mass photographs as one striated body from the flexor retinaculum to the thumb. Run with the merge off, the marker watershed claimed it for one seed at a time: APB appears on 16, FPB on 23 and OP on 19 of the 44 levels that have MC1, i.e. the three regions swap identity from level to level instead of forming three continuous bellies (this thumb lies off the palm, so the seeds' textbook offsets from MC1 often land in the thumb's fat or outside the palm's tissue island, and no pale septum runs through the thenar mass at most levels). Their union, 11.3 cm3, is a plausible thenar group (10-20 cm3); the parts, 3.6 / 6.1 / 1.5 cm3, are not trustworthy as named muscles.
